target.title: Improve long reset countdown precision
target.body:
## Summary

`resetCountdownDescription` (`UsageFormatter.swift`) drops minutes — and even hours —
once a countdown crosses into days:

```swift
if days > 0 {
    if hours > 0 { return "in \(days)d \(hours)h" }
    return "in \(days)d"
}
if hours > 0 {
    if minutes > 0 { return "in \(hours)h \(minutes)m" }
    return "in \(hours)h"
}
```

The hours-tier already shows both units when non-zero (`"in 3h 31m"`), but the days-tier
never shows minutes, and silently collapses to just `"in 5d"` whenever there happen to be
zero whole hours (e.g. a reset 5 days and 37 minutes out reads as "in 5d", indistinguishable
from a reset exactly 5 days out).

Extends the days branch to match the existing hours branch: show whichever of
hours/minutes are non-zero.

- `in 5d` — unchanged, exact days
- `in 5d 12h` — unchanged, exact hours
- `in 5d 12h 34m` — new, previously silently dropped the minutes
- `in 5d 37m` — new, previously collapsed to `in 5d` when whole hours were zero

This affects every place `ResetTimeDisplayStyle.countdown` renders a "Resets in …" string:
menu bar, CLI, widget.

## Test plan

- [x] Extended `UsageFormatterTests.swift` with 4 new/updated cases covering exact days,
      days+exact-hours, days+hours+minutes, and days+minutes-without-whole-hours.
- [x] `swift test --filter UsageFormatterTests` — 40/40 pass.
- [x] `swiftformat --lint` / `swiftlint --strict` on changed files — 0 violations.
- [x] `swift build` — clean.
